earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only survey/wordlist material (Hallberg 1992 Languages of Indus Kohistan; Rensch 1992 wordlists/texts); no grammar or phonology of Bateri found.

sources.note: Bateri article is a stub citing only Ethnologue and FLI; Indus Kohistani article mentions Bateri as 'a closely related dialect or language variety' and has no stress/tone content.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x. Languoid page Bateri (bate1261); reference record 132470 (Hallberg 1992).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference at all; refs are Hallberg 1992 and Bashir 2003 (subclassification), Campbell et al. 2022 and Rahman 2006 (endangerment). Alt names Batera Kohistani, Baterawal, Bateri Kohistani, Dardu.

sources.citation: Forum for Language Initiatives (FLI), Islamabad. 'Bateri' language-community page (2021); news posts 'Planning for preservation of Bateri Language started' (2021-10-14) and 'Breakthrough in Literature Development for Three Indigenous Languages: Balti, Kalkoti and Bateri' (2024-07-11).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. States the language 'lacks a functional writing system', that documentation began with a 2021 vitality survey, that community researcher Muhammad Baqi is collaborating with an unnamed international researcher, and that Bateri had its first (untitled) publication in 2024. FLI publication pages list no Bateri title.

sources.citation: Liljegren, Henrik et al. 2021. Hindu Kush Areal Typology, CLDF dataset v1.0. Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.7139828.
sources.note: Downloaded and checked: Bateri (btv/bate1261) is not among the sampled languages in, so no HKAT prosody data for Bateri; the zip was deleted from the Bateri folder.

sources.citation: Baart, Joan L.G. 2003. Tonal features in languages of northern Pakistan. In J.L.G. Baart & G.H. Sindhi (eds.), Pakistani languages and society: problems and prospects, 132-144. Islamabad: NIPS & SIL. (FLI web offprint, 13 pp., own pagination)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Table 1 (offprint p. 2): '2. Bateri Yes? 30,000' where 'a question mark indicates that I am not certain about the status of the language as to tone'; Table 3 (p. 6) lists 'Bateri?' under the Shina-type (defined pp. 9-10 as lexical stress on one mora, H tone supplied by rule). No Bateri data given; a tentative guess, not a description.

sources.citation: Hallberg, Daniel G. 1992. The languages of Indus Kohistan. In C.R. Rensch, S.J. Decker & D.G. Hallberg (eds.), Languages of Kohistan (Sociolinguistic Survey of Northern Pakistan 1), 83-141 (ch. 5 'Bateri', pp. 133-141). Islamabad: NIPS & SIL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 5 covers lexical similarity (58-61% with Indus Kohistani, 29-30% with Shina), recorded-text testing, dialect opinion and vitality only; sec. 2.2.3 (p. 96): 'The scope of this report does not cover the phonology'; p. 133: 'very little has been said about this language group'.

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 1992. Indus Kohistan Word Lists (Appendix D.1, pp. 207-225; column BAT = Bateri, Batera village, reliability B) and Indus Kohistani Texts (Appendix D.2.7 'Bateri, Batera', pp. 249-251). In Languages of Kohistan (SSNP 1). Islamabad: NIPS & SIL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Raw data only. Symbol key p. 147 lists ['] = stress; the mark appears irregularly on Bateri items (su'rVt 'body', nV'thur 'nose', hàK'gwi 'finger', hàlà'li 'heart', 'làKgRi 'door', mu'sum, bà'là in the text) with no rule stated; p. 146: the lists and texts 'are field transcriptions and have not undergone thorough phonological and grammatical analysis'.

sources.citation: Forum for Language Initiatives / Muhammad Baqi. 2024. First Bateri-language publication (title not given on the FLI site), and FLI Bateri documentation materials 2021-.
